reviews.text: In the foul blackness of the far future, there is only conflict

[b]While the game is fun,[/b] I have a list of gripes: 1. Still can not sell spare munitions or crew. 2. Attacking merchants is less rewarding that random encounters despite being better equipped to fight you. 3. Not all attack types have station based counters, to make things arbitrarily difficult rather than logically difficult. 4. Factions are just flavor that exist only to offer you units, but still attack you and act like any other enemy. 5. You can not upgrade units to higher tier versions of themselves, leaving you with many useless Tier 1 units later on who do not get stronger. [b]Suggestions,[/b] to go along with the list of gripes: 1. Add the ability to sell off munitions and crew to traders. 2. Make it so attacking merchants rewards you with normal loot + and a item from their normal sale list. As piracy in this game should be unrestricted. 3. There should be a point defense turret sub-system you can find, or a turret slot weapon that is anti-missile, asteroid, etc. Functioning as a shield that can stop a certain number of shield ignoring attacks per charge. Balancing itself by taking up a weapon slot or subsystem slot along with its energy cost. 4. Encounters with allied faction are far less likely to be combat, and more likely to be interactive encounters or assist in combat encounters. So the factions territory feels like more of a Role Play / Friendly zone. 5. The idea that a necromancer can not become a greater necromancer, imperial soldier can not become a martial, imperial acolyte can not become a imperial scribe. etc. The idea that very obvious unit progression exists, but no way to pay to promote units is very odd. This could be added as an option at stations or at traders.

It's basically FTL in a different universe, honestly feels like an FTL mod. FTL is an amazing game and maybe Void War will see the introduction of a new steam tag - 'FTL-like'. The game mechanics are pretty much the same with the added focus on crew optimisation which adds atmosphere and different play styles. I mentioned FTL 5 times so I think if you enjoy FTL (6), you'll enjoy Void War!
建议买之前体验体验demo。 目前做的做好的flt-like游戏。缝合了点40k。 新的系统包括角色装备和灵能没有无人机。 目前内容太多了，随机性过头了。导致难度非常看运气。前期刷不到合适武器就可以重开了。 目前价格有点小贵，50差不多。 关于中文问题，作者说看销量。这游戏英文是一方面问题另一个问题是大量使用哥特体看的头大。
RNG部分还行，通关一次就可以用死亡骑士+欧格林船长的轮椅组合，开局直送两个140hp的大哥跳帮乱杀。 高难度最大的问题是数值有点崩，大后期升满船还有几百碎片买不到好的组件和船员，对射射不过，跳帮对面一堆神选大魔，憋屈到死。 总的来讲比demo强了一丢丢，补足了不少内容，但体感还是FTL+40K的mod加强版，50左右可入。

I was excited for this one, because FTL is one of the best games I've played, but despite it is 120% identical to FTL, i didn't enjoy it that much. There is no exploration element, which made FTL for me so magical. You don't have fuel system and you only move forward. Also encounters are almost always attack you. So it is not that interesting. Maybe I played too little, and had higher expectations for this game. Edit. I was a little frustrated and agree, that my review was not well formated and I contradict myself. So here is more coherent review. TL;DR; this game lacks content and thought This game is FTL in form, but not by soul. What do I mean is that in FTL I were so much more excited to explore as much as possible in sectors, and the constant pressure of lowering fuel was such a nice detail. I mean yeah i have only three fuel to jump away, and the fleet is approaching, but there is a distress signal, sooo. In comparison, here it feels like "there is only war" and not much more. Yeah there are paths too technically, but you only go forward, and most of the times you can choose only one path to see something interesting, so it feels like a linear game with facade. There are a lot of weapons and some redesigned systems. Personally I really liked health and personnel fight mechanics here. That was really fun(except for the weapon that summons ghouls or whatever, that help you in battle, except they clog your health regen room, and you can't control them to gtfo from there, so you can heal your staff) And for the WH40k part. It doesn't make sense at all. There are no meta politics, like some factions are more friendly, some are not, some have allies and disliked factions. Here it just feels too shallow. You can hire anyone and everyone is so chill with each other. I understand, that in FTL I could do the same, but these factions were not from WH40k. And if you copy so blatantly from another source, there would be implications from players like me, that these factions should be at least a little bit similar to the original ones. For the visuals, I liked clean choice in FTL more. The style is good here, artists did a great job, but I just don't like the color scheme, everything is grey-♥♥♥♥ color. But still visuals are nice, even though i don't like them Overall this game has potential, but lacks depth and content. I think I will wait for some time and then play FTL Multiverse again, because I don't believe that something will change here

I rarely give negative reviews, but this one earned one. There is simply no creativity in this one, no voice overs, no story - nothing of value at all. It is just an ugly FTL clone, with no improvements, not even utilizing the overly obvious Warhammer 40k lore inspiration to any advantage.

It's an FTL mod that strips down the event system to the point of not being worth reading after a run, and which fails to credit FTL while lifting every single ship upgrade progression directly from that game. The 20$ price tag is an insult.

Excellent legally distinct game set in the gloomy murk of a distant indeterminate timeframe. Where there is a notable presence of armed conflict. In terms of comparisons to FTL: 1. The setting and tone are very different. A much bleaker setting that takes heavy inspiration from certain... popular dark sci-fi universes. 2. Mechanically and UI-wise, it's incredibly similar to FTL. Even identical in some areas. This may or may not be to your taste. 3. Very different from vanilla FTL in a number of significant ways. Boarding is much more important, there is a wider array of base game content. Psychic powers, individual crew gear, and main character-esque commanders are major additions. This is a substantially more mechanically complex game than vanilla FTL. Basically, this is a game that you'll really enjoy if you loved FTL and like dark sci-fi. if you want an entirely original underlying game system or setting, this one will miss you. The writing and storytelling are passable, but haven't made any leaps FTL. The game is mechanically rich and otherwise very enjoyable.

This is just my opinion, and if you enjoy the game, I’m genuinely happy for you! I was really excited for an FTL-like game set in a legally distinct 400 Warmaces universe. Before launch, I saw plenty of people upset that Void War looked like an FTL clone, but personally I didn’t care. FTL came out ages ago, and it felt like high time for a spiritual successor. I assumed that by copying the formula, the devs could take advantage of the time saved to focus on adding new ideas and expanding it. So, my negative review has nothing to do with the similarities to FTL. I wanted this game to succeed and be awesome. Like many, I spent a gazillion hours on FTL, and then another gazillion on the excellent (and free if you have FTL) Multiverse mod. Given that Void War is a 20€ game and copies so much from FTL, I expected it to improve and innovate not just on FTL, but also on what Multiverse had achieved. I thought that was a fair assumption, why copy so much of the original game without trying to push the formula further from what was already available out there? After a few hours with Void War, I realized that in the grim darkness of the far future, there is only boarding and missiles. This limited strategic variety felt like a massive step down, not just from FTL, but especially from Multiverse. Yes, boarding and missiles are more in-depth here, and I’ll give credit where it’s due: Void War brings some quality-of-life improvements to ship management during battles. But compared to everything that’s missing, it’s like a grain of sand. Void War has fewer playable races, fewer ship systems, fewer nodes to explore, fewer unique or story-driven encounters, fewer encounters overall, fewer weapons and fewer ships. That’s a lot of "less" especially at a 20€ price point. I prefer to give money to the devs, even for mods, my gripe is the price/quantity/innovation over what we already have, it's just not there. I think it’s fair to compare Void War (a full game that you can buy) to Multiverse (a mod) because it’s widely known among FTL fans, and the devs surely knew it existed. Yet they chose not to innovate beyond it and charged a premium price (for a game like this) on top of that. To me, that feels like adding insult to injury and I honestly can’t recommend the game unless it's on sale. I feel like I played a mod, not a 1.0 version of a full game. Sadly this isn't an EA game with a roadmap, it's a full-priced game with a roadmap, and the idea of waiting for upgrades or potentially paid DLC for a promise to get the full experience further leaves a bad taste in my mouth.

Is this a FTL Clone? Mostly. Do I care? Not really. Why? It's FTL and Warhammer shoved into one greasy cheese burger. Is it good for me? No. But will I eat it? Obviously, who would waste a perfectly good cheeseburger??? If you enjoyed FTL, you will know the majority of inns and outs, however be warned, boarding combat is WAY more inclusive in this game than it was in FTL, so keep that in mind. If you like Warhammer, the vibe of this game is spot on, even the music gives you that dystopian space imperialistic decay that the WH universe has. Overall, I hope this game just continues to generate content, because it's really good.

I am not one of the people who shun this game for being an FTL clone, in fact I was hoping that it was. The only reason I bought this game was BECAUSE I wanted it to be a fresh version of FTL but unfortunately it comes way short of that. It's difficult to pinpoint exactly why it feels so empty but there are a few obvious missteps. 1. Your crew is replaceable and completely lacks value. The reason for this is because crew does not gain experience like they did in FTL, instead the only investment you can make in your crew is equipment such as weapons armor and tools. But that's just not enough for me to care. Losing a crew member in this game is a minor inconvenience compared to the potentially run-ending event that it was in FTL. 2. Unlocking ships is linear and BORING. All you have to do to unlock the next ship is win a run with the previous one, or just outright purchase it with points. In practice this means that you'll often find yourself doing the same builds/strategies, focusing solely on winning rather than exploring the game. In comparison, FTL had unique unlock-conditions for most ships, that forced the player to deviate from the 'standard' builds/strategies and in doing so, made the game more fun and engaging in the long-term. 3. Lacking weapons. This one really hurts. You would think that the successor to FTL would have more weapons and new, creative ways of addressing combat and yet somehow it ended up having less. The new subsystems that they've added are either 'Weapons' turned into subsystems, for example the laser and bombarding systems, or they are just cheap novelties that don't do much, like the clone-bay and the crew-stun systems. (Don't quote me on the names, I can't be bothered to open the game and check) And when it comes to actual weapons, they all feel samey. You have your normal Shooter, Ion, Laser and Missiles(Moved into a subsystem for some reason????), no innovation compared to FTL but even worse, the variety in each weapon category is less than what FTL had to offer. 4. Tediously long runs. Because the game is so empty and samey, the runs feel like an absolute chore. Several times, I've found myself thinking that I'm close to the final boss, only to open up the map and, with a heavy sigh of boredom and disappointment, realize that I'm merely half-way through the run. I have a total of 300+ hours in FTL on multiple accounts and I loved every second of it and yet after playing 20 hours of Void War, I already feel like I've seen everything this game has to offer and cannot bring myself to boot it up again. TL;DR The only reason I bought this game was because I read all the reviews that said 'If you love FTL, buy this game'. Well, I do love FTL and I most certainly do not love this game. This does not come even close to filling FTL's boots, no matter how much I wanted it to.

Evasion is borked. I'm missing 3/4 shots EVERY CYCLE to ships that have 25% evasion. Late game is impossible even with a good build and full upgrades because you simply cannot hit shots.

The developers of Void War have given us a (very much a legally distinct) FTL-style Warhammer game in which you can: - Recruit legally distinct Space Marines and have them fight alongside psyker cultists and demonspawn; - Raid and pillage the ruins within the not-Eye of Chaos, for the glory of the Chaos Gods with a squad of not-Mechanicus battle droids; - Run a warship with a skeleton crew, while suicide charging the enemy ships with waves of electrified servitors; - Kill an entire room with a legally distinct Nurgle Space Marine fart cloud and have nearby allies actively benefitting from its poisonous effect. Games Workshop, eat your heart out. Okay, now since the not-Emperor is dead on his not-Golden Throne and the not-Imperium of Man is crumbling, when do I get to 1v1 not-Horus?

Close, very close to being the successor to FTL(Faster Than Light) with 40k flavor. But they missed the mark. Much like you will if you try to play this game. What do I mean? Well let me tell you. You will miss shots , impossible amounts of shots in sequence that turn an hour long run into a meaningless death. because the game arbitrarily decided you are unable to land a single shot ... and it is maddening. I don't want to have to micro every single volley to allow my ship to do literally 1 damage to an enemy ship to finish a simple non boss fight ( this exact scenario has happened 2 runs in a row for no apparent reason, beat a ship till its 1 health and it becomes immortal with its dodge when i launch a volley of 8 non fusilade shots and 5 to land to break the shield and end it and it just won't ). - Some people will tell me thats just bad luck and i don't disagree but for the love of God don't bake that into your game. FTL did this better. I love difficulty with my rogue like's. It's what makes them fun. This even has a similar and more deep progression system to FTL. But its all just lipstick on a pig if they cannot fix the miss chances.

The game rewards you for leaning into unhinged builds and WILL crush you if you don't have a plan on later difficulties. If you're on the fence, trust me, it's worth it.

游戏还不错，比FTL多了诸如重力控制器之类可以影响船员属性的许多飞船子系统，人物有战士法师和苦力之分，还有许多飞船强化能力、人物装备和技能系统。飞船武器种类和强度相比较弱，而且敌人护盾充能很快，闪避率也高，武器基本要齐射才能打的出伤害，单靠自动发射效率极低。相比之下，人物技能无视护盾而且不会miss，登陆跳帮可以瞬间召回，所以游戏比FTL更加侧重跳帮战、人物技能和飞船子系统的使用策略，更考验微操。游戏后期需要兼顾飞船损管、人物移动、跳帮战斗、技能发动等等许多操作，虽然可以在暂停状态下操作，但是整体难度依然不低，而且后期敌人的数值和跳帮强度也非常高，根本打不起消耗战。 目前玩下来缺点一是没有中文，二是船员人数稍微多一些的话，管理的时候就需要翻页，如果需要看血量、找人、发动技能等等就显得非常混乱。

This is a great but also infuriating game at times. Sometimes, you'll think, "hmm, I want to play a rapid fire gun game", and the every shop you go to will have all the guns you want. But other games you'll think "hmm, since I unlocked this ship which buffs demonic summons, I'll run a game around that", only for every psychic shop to decide to sell only debuff and poison spells. And then of course, the first shop you run into next game, when running a different build, will have summoners and summon spells, despite it not even being a psychic shop.

Honestly this game is pretty solid overall, but it's got two major flaws that make me give it the thumbs down. 1. They took the worst part of FTL, the boss get stronger if you do too well and kill the crew, and applied it to not only the bosses but mini-bosses and partially to just some random encounter ships. FTL already had the issue that too many builds that would get you through the entire game easily would flail uselessly against the boss because killing crew was a bad approach. The demon ships in this just take that to 11. Can't use fire, can't use poison, can't use suffocation, can't use boarders outside of a few very limited options, can't break systems... a significant numbers of builds just go right out the window against a demon ship, which all bosses will turn into at a certain point. 2. I know it's a cliche thing for gamers to complain about at this point, but the RNG in this is actually broken and/or lying. It's not hard to test, load up on shields quickly and there are plenty of early fights that can't hurt you, so you can sit for a while tallying hits and misses. Enemy ships are 50-100% more evasive than they list, at evasion 20 vs. 100 shots the ships I tested against would dodge 30-40 shots. And your ship is roughly half as evasive as listed, 20 evasion vs. 100 shots had me dodge ~10. With shields being the only viable defense and so many offensive options hitting a wall on bosses and demon ship encounters expect a lot of your builds to start to look the same.

It's a game which comes across as challenging fun and I've put a fair amount of hours into it. However progress is none existent with a player missing out on much of what the game offers in weapons, power ups and set up's unless they wish to play on maximum difficulty levels. Starting from the bottom it is nigh on impossible to level up what ships are available to you to select for your next run as nothing bar a couple of ships from the next level unlocks. Same with weapons, powers and starting crew. Then you have the demonic ships / final bosses which require a particular set up to beat, so no variation in tactics if you havent been able to find these weapons / crew during the run. So you get killed off eager to start again, to find that effort has only slowly ticked towards unlocking something. Yes you can refer to cheat codes and cheat engines to fix the games issues with difficulty / progress but whats the point in that, only to see what lies further. So, after initially being impressed at so much the devs have done right, at its heart the game structure / progress / difficulty levelling is broken.

Friendly crew, including the player commander, die instantly if aboard the enemy ship at the time of its destruction. That might seem "realistic", but in light of the always-available and free "Recall Crew" button that instantly teleports back all friendly crew from the enemy ship, this insta-death mechanic is actually just a glaring QoL hole. Why make players click a button in a scenario where they'd want to click it 100% of the time? Such anti-player "gotcha" design feels bad to play with, especially when it causes commander death and ends a long run. It doesn't help that ships can receive hull damage from a myriad of sources: fire, asteroids, the psychic missiles that you initiated 14 in-game seconds ago but you've since forgotten because it's been 5 busy minutes and there's no progress bar to help you keep track of when those are finally going to fire. These can quickly overwhelm the visual clarity of the user interface, which already struggles to communicate low enemy hull durability - those little violet sparks are easily lost in the visual noise. Worse yet, some environmental / boss effects actually white-out the entire screen briefly, including non-diegetic HUD elements. This leaves me between a laborious and an unfun place: must I be hypervigilant about boarding, or must I simply abandon that mechanic? Let crewmates auto-recall on ship destruction, or let zero-hull ships remain intact for a couple seconds for manual recall. The alternative is that If we can't get auto-recall, then at least zero-hull ships should remain intact for 2 seconds. I don't find this to be gamebreaking, but the cumulation of this and other pain points leads me to disagree that Void War should be rated 94% positive. I'd probably call it 75-80% positive, though. If that meets your bar, give the demo a try. [hr][/hr] Other pain points: Why are there no time speed options? Repeatedly double-tapping spacebar is a poor replacement for quarter or half-speed controls. Why can't I view important information on items (namely psychograms), summons, and abilities until they're irreversibly purchased / installed? Why are all event choices so irritatingly opaque? Sure, FTL's events weren't much clearer, but I'll give FTL some leeway on account of it having pioneered this genre. There are massive difficulty spikes from encountering enemy crews comprised of five to eight summoners who each can spawn two to five mobs directly onto your ship - it seems the game considers such a crew equivalent to a small number of strong units, but a 50-ghoul bumrush inundating your ship is infinitely more threatening and less counterable than three Death Knights sitting on their own ship, not to mention that the summoner crew also benefits from more hands to repair away your own damage and effects. [hr][/hr] Side note, isn't it curious that everyone's hyper-aware of possible legal action from Games Workshop, but basically nobody is considering similar action from Subset Games, who owns - functionally speaking - the far more impactful source content? What makes grimdark worldbuilding more intellectually protectable than the entire core design of a game, including UX, art style, and all fundamental gameplay mechanics?

57 hours played. I should probably talk about the combat, ship customization, crew management, and all the other reasons this game is fantastic. Instead, let me tell you about my last run. My commander was a cannibal. At one point I boarded an enemy ship that had a husk rack continuously spawning weak enemies. This was apparently a tactical mistake on their part. What started as a boarding action quickly became a feeding frenzy. By the time the husk rack stopped providing tasty crunchy beep-boop snacks, my commander had stacked himself to over 30 DPS and was basically skipping his tubby ass through the enemy ship beating people to death with the enthusiasm of a sugar high toddler running through a candy store. The enemy crew did not survive. Fresh off this glorious victory, I answered a distress signal. A small colony needed medical assistance. One of their settlers was critically ill. Being the benevolent hero that I am, I used my fully upgraded medical bay to save her life. She immediately gave birth. Unfortunately the baby was... wrong. Horrifically wrong. The colonists took one look at the screaming eldritch nightmare that had emerged from their companion, collectively decided this was now my problem, shoved me back toward my ship, dropped the abomination at my feet, and practically locked the airlock behind me. This is how I became the unwilling adoptive parent of a blightling named "Cthulga." I kept waiting for the little bastard to die. She did not. Boarding actions? Survived. Space battles? Survived. Ancient horrors? Survived. Against all logic, reason, and probably several laws of nature, Cthulga made it all the way to the Vault of Souls and stood with us at the end of our victorious journey. 10/10. Came for grimdark spaceship combat. Left with a cannibal war hero and a custody arrangement I never agreed to.

Yes, it's an improvement over a 13 year old game it is based on. You shouldn't play it because the developer is apparently disrespectful to you. [h3]Anime in Void War[/h3] A small part of the game's content is intentionally imbued with distinctive aspects of one sci-fi anime series (and so it constitutes a "parody" of it): [spoiler]Neon Genesis Evangelion[/spoiler] ... [spoiler]It's in the form of humans operating ships, described as having arrived from another universe or dimension.[/spoiler] The overall similarity doesn't reach legal infringement threshold and the differences include that the humans are not drawn in an anime style. The shared aspects include: [spoiler]The human group is called SDF and possesses superior technology (like the SSDF in NGE does). The humans' faces have similarities with faces of pilots in NGE, most notable one their apparent age. They lack the natives' psionic abilities and they are superior at operating combat craft. The appearance of the group's ships is reminiscent of that of non-human living beings in NGE.[/spoiler] Even though the appearances of this content take up a tiny portion of the game, it is common to experience them at least once per "run". [i]("Run" is an instance of playing the game from the start to the end. This game is designed to be short but played many times)[/i]. The insertion of this content eradicates the primacy of Void War's own world, reducing it to one of the two worlds within the game. That's one reason why I wouldn't like it even if I loved the anime. The NGE-themed group is portrayed as the winner in the conflict between it and the natives of Void War (even though it is not a big challenge for the player). The insertion of this constitutes an assertion of dominance over the player by the developer. The first time it is encountered, it is a "pie in the face". All subsequent times it is encountered are instances of the player choosing to be dominated and humiliated by the developer again, as if choosing to kiss the developer's foot, just so that he can continue to derive enjoyment from the game. [hr][/hr] [h3]Who made Void War?[/h3] The game is said to be made by "Tundra", and there's been noticeable scarcity of places with an explanation as to who "Tundra" represents [i](one such place being the endgame credits)[/i]. I can do no more than to invite you to reflect on this. [hr][/hr] [h3]Other thoughts[/h3] The game uses up a lot of CPU power for a 2D game. It panders to new players in distasteful ways, of which the most glaring example is that the tutorial difficulty is called 'Normal'. The game does come with a few good, non-obvious ideas, of which the most significant one is the realization that a (borderline) grimdark setting is a good match for FTL's game mechanics. There is more that I could criticize Void War for, but I don't want to effectively provide advice on how to improve the game. The game is rotten at its core, irrespective of how fun or polished it may seem. Don't demean yourself by giving it your time and attention.
